clue.text: Craft's able to bridge a river

indicators.note: to bridge something is to span it from both sides, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: able means can, as in 'I can'
the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in south-west England

explanation.surface: A boat is capable of spanning a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bridge' signals one piece spanning the other; the river is on the Devon-Cornwall border, and the 's after Craft is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, and a boat is a craft.

clue.text: Single-minded?

parts.note: read as 'minded to stay single', describing someone who has chosen not to marry

explanation.definitionFit: Someone celibate abstains from marriage and sex, so in a pun they have a mind to remain single.

clue.text: In retrospect, it answers the big one

annotationWithheld.why: In retrospect, it answers the big one (5) for TITAN: reversing IT gives TI, but no reading of 'answers' gives TAN or the rest of the reversed letters
annotationWithheld.clue: In retrospect, it answers the big one

clue.text: Thousand, plus one number, put in order for fruit

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
plus means and

indicators.note: put in says these pieces are inserted into the word for order

parts.note: to order things is to arrange them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Instructions to sort a thousand items plus one more into some sequence for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places the one and the number after the first two letters of the order word, making ARINORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin orange is a small citrus fruit, also called a tangerine.

clue.text: Trusting in later development

indicators.note: a development of letters is a working-up of them into a new form, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone trusts in what will develop later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges the seven letters of IN LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reliant on something means depending on it, which is trusting in it.

clue.text: Civet cat lives and is protected

indicators.note: what is protected is held within the other piece, so the word and goes inside

parts.note: a cat proverbially has nine lives
taken as written

explanation.surface: A civet cat is alive and kept safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is protected' wraps the cat's proverbial lives round 'and', which fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The nandine is the African palm civet, a small tree-dwelling civet cat.

clue.text: Shred of straw is paltry

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters come from inside the next words

explanation.surface: A scrap of straw is a trivial thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' takes the run across stra(W IS P)altry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a thin strand or small fragment, much like a shred.

clue.text: Elected because half were faked

parts.note: a candidate elected is in
since means because

indicators.note: half tells us to drop part of the word were, keeping only its second half

explanation.surface: Someone won office because half the votes were rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts WE from WERE to leave RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere feelings are put on or pretended, so they are faked rather than genuine.

clue.text: Like more money to pass on

parts.note: P stands for penny or pence, a small sum of British money
to refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else

explanation.surface: Someone would rather pass on money to others.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer one thing is to like it more than another.

clue.text: Cleaning room to sort out jumble

indicators.note: sort out means rearrange, so the preceding letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Tidying a room in order to clear up a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' rearranges CLEANING ROOM TO; the 'to' that reads as part of the instruction is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomeration is a mixed mass of things gathered together, a jumble.

clue.text: It's heads on American quarter and tails on thieves' dog

definitions.text: It's heads on American quarter and tails on thieves' dog

parts.words: It's heads on American quarter and tails on thieves' dog
parts.note: the language of the motto E Pluribus Unum on US coins, and the word following both thieves' and dog in names of debased jargon

explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' and 'tails' play on coin-tossing; the language heads the quarter's motto and tails the phrases thieves' ... and dog ... (slang and mock versions of it).
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the language of US coin mottoes and appears in the phrases thieves' Latin and dog Latin.

clue.text: Spiny lobster becomes gelatinous without one

indicators.note: becomes signals that the letters turn into something new, an anagram

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lobster turns to jelly when one is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one' takes I out of GELATINOUS; 'becomes' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Langouste is the French name used for the spiny lobster, a clawless crustacean.

clue.text: First two swapped neckwear

annotationWithheld.why: First two swapped neckwear (7) for BANDANA: B AND A gives the first two letters swapped, but no parse supplies the final NA

clue.text: Genuine problem for naive girl

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in a mess, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A real difficulty for an unworldly young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stage role.

clue.text: To notice where chip can finish dish

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
in golf a chip shot can end up in the hole

explanation.surface: A notice showing where a chip might end up on a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Chip suggests chips on a plate, but it is the golf shot. TOAD IN THE HOLE is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad-in-the-hole is a traditional British dish of sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter.

clue.text: Well ground in hearing range

annotationWithheld.why: Well ground in hearing range (9) for AMPLITUDE: no reading of 'well ground in hearing' found that builds the letters

clue.text: Swipe your old underhand

parts.note: to swipe is to steal
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Snatching your old possessions in a sly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy actions are done furtively and secretly, so they are underhand.

clue.text: Substitute for something binding in declaration

parts.note: a pronoun such as it stands in for a noun naming something
cement is a binding material

explanation.surface: A stand-in for a binding agreement appears in a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is a formal statement, a declaration.

clue.text: Once a pen

parts.note: a means one, a single
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: A pen that once existed.
explanation.definitionFit: Onefold means single or happening one time, which is what once describes.

clue.text: Literally any one in state's downfall

indicators.note: the word any is rendered in letters, since the letter names N E sound like it

parts.note: said as letter names, N E sounds like any

indicators.note: in places one inside the word for a sorry state

parts.note: a mess is a state, as in a terrible state
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Literally anyone could cause a state's collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' asks for the word any written as the letter names that sound like it; 'in' puts one inside the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is a person or thing bringing about someone's ruin, their downfall.

clue.text: Place for hanging up large stake

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: large means big
a stake is a bet

explanation.surface: Somewhere to hang up a big wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is a gallows, a structure for hanging criminals.

clue.text: Take off a couple without it

parts.note: a means one, which is I in Roman numerals

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other letters go around it

parts.note: to couple is to mate
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remove a pair of things without it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the couple wraps round 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, which is to imitate.

clue.text: Pain of my queenless country

indicators.note: queenless means without the queen, ER, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Algeria is a North African country

explanation.surface: The pain of my country losing its queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is a common crossword queen; 'queenless' takes it from ALGERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Myalgia is the medical term for muscle pain.

clue.text: Iceberg holds back diver

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse
the word holds contains a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: An iceberg conceals a diver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' takes EBERG from icEBERG; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving waterbird, and a diver is a bird that dives.

clue.text: To jeer about prompting is conventional

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece encloses the next

parts.note: to jeer is to boo
an urge is a prompting, an inner push
taken as written

explanation.surface: Booing someone for prompting is a conventional reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the jeer round the prompting, leaving the last O of the jeer after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourgeois describes middle-class conventional attitudes and tastes.

clue.text: Still fit in less seconds

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to fit something in is to insert it

explanation.surface: Still managing to fit in less in a few seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, unmoving, which is still.

clue.text: One stringing a line

definitions.meaning: someone who ties or strings things together
a row or rank, as of seats in a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or layer, and literally one who ties is a tier.

clue.text: Gut reaction

parts.note: read literally, a reaction of the gut or intestines rather than an instinctive feeling

explanation.definitionFit: Dysentery is an infection of the intestines, quite literally the bowels reacting badly.
